clauseText: Payment Terms. Client shall pay Contractor the agreed-upon fee within thirty (30) days of receiving a valid invoice. Invoices shall be submitted upon completion of each milestone or on a monthly basis, as mutually agreed. Late payments shall accrue interest at a rate of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is lower. Either party may dispute an invoice in good faith by providing written notice within fifteen (15) days of receipt, and the undisputed portion shall remain due.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement and Freelancers Union model contract

clauseText: Scope of Work. Contractor shall perform the services described in the attached Statement of Work (SOW). Any work beyond the scope of the SOW shall require a written change order signed by both parties before work begins. The change order shall specify the additional scope, timeline adjustment, and any additional fees. Contractor is not obligated to perform work outside the agreed scope without an executed change order.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement

clauseText: Intellectual Property. Upon full payment of all fees due, Contractor assigns to Client all right, title, and interest in the work product created under this Agreement, excluding Contractor's pre-existing intellectual property and general knowledge, skills, and experience. Contractor retains the right to use general tools, techniques, and methodologies developed or refined during the engagement. Contractor grants Client a perpetual, non-exclusive license to any pre-existing IP incorporated into the deliverables.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement and AIGA standard design contract

clauseText: Confidentiality. Each party agrees to hold the other party's Confidential Information in strict confidence and not to disclose it to third parties except as necessary to perform obligations under this Agreement, and only to individuals bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as those herein. Confidential Information does not include information that is publicly available, independently developed, or rightfully received from a third party without restriction. This obligation survives termination for a period of two (2) years.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper mutual NDA and standard freelance terms

clauseText: Indemnification. Each party shall indemnify and hold harmless the other party from and against any third-party claims, losses, damages, and reasonable expenses (including attorneys' fees) arising from (a) the indemnifying party's breach of this Agreement, (b) the indemnifying party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (c) the indemnifying party's violation of applicable law. The indemnified party shall provide prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation in the defense of any claim.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper balanced indemnification clause

clauseText: Limitation of Liability. Neither party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages arising out of or related to this Agreement, regardless of the theory of liability. Each party's total cumulative liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. This limitation does not apply to breaches of confidentiality obligations or indemnification duties.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement

clauseText: Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within fifteen (15) days of receiving written notice thereof. Upon termination, Client shall pay Contractor for all work completed and accepted through the effective date of termination.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement

clauseText: Dispute Resolution. The parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute arising out of this Agreement through informal negotiation. If the dispute cannot be resolved within thirty (30) days, either party may initiate mediation administered by a mutually agreed-upon mediator. If mediation fails to resolve the dispute within sixty (60) days, either party may pursue binding arbitration under the rules of the American Arbitration Association. Each party shall bear its own costs of mediation and arbitration.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper dispute resolution framework

clauseText: Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the state in which the Client is headquartered, without regard to conflict of laws principles. Both parties consent to the personal jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in that state for any actions not subject to arbitration.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement

clauseText: Non-Solicitation. During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither party shall directly solicit for employment any employee or contractor of the other party who was involved in the performance of this Agreement, without the prior written consent of the other party. This restriction does not apply to general job postings or unsolicited applications. This clause does not restrict Contractor from performing services for Client's competitors.
sourceAttribution: Based on Freelancers Union model terms — balanced non-solicitation without non-compete

clauseText: Warranties. Contractor represents and warrants that (a) Contractor has the right and authority to enter into this Agreement, (b) the work product will be original and will not infringe upon the intellectual property rights of any third party, and (c) the services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards. Client represents and warrants that Client has the right and authority to enter into this Agreement and that materials provided by Client for use in the work product do not infringe third-party rights.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement

clauseText: Force Majeure. Neither party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform its obligations under this Agreement due to causes beyond its reasonable control, including but not limited to acts of God, natural disasters, pandemic, war, terrorism, government action, power failure, internet disruption, or labor disputes. The affected party shall provide prompt written notice and use reasonable efforts to mitigate the impact. If the force majeure event continues for more than sixty (60) days, either party may terminate this Agreement without liability.
sourceAttribution: Based on standard commercial force majeure language

clauseText: Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may assign this Agreement to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement

clauseText: Notice. All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed given when delivered personally, sent by email with confirmation of receipt, or sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses specified in this Agreement. Either party may change its notice address by providing written notice to the other party in accordance with this section.
sourceAttribution: Based on standard commercial notice provisions

clauseText: Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended or modified except by a written instrument signed by both parties. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving party. A waiver of any breach shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach.
sourceAttribution: Based on Common Paper Standard Freelance Agreement

clauseText: Insurance. Contractor shall maintain, at Contractor's own expense, professional liability insurance (errors and omissions) with coverage of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and general commercial liability insurance with coverage of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence. Contractor shall provide certificates of insurance upon Client's reasonable request.
sourceAttribution: Based on standard professional services insurance requirements

clauseText: Rent Payment. Tenant shall pay monthly rent in the amount specified in this Lease on or before the first (1st) day of each calendar month. Rent shall be payable by check, electronic transfer, or other method mutually agreed upon. A late fee of five percent (5%) of the monthly rent may be charged if rent is received more than five (5) days after the due date. Landlord shall provide a receipt upon Tenant's request.
sourceAttribution: Based on HUD model lease and tenant advocacy organizations' balanced templates

clauseText: Termination. Either party may terminate this Lease at the end of the initial term or any renewal term by providing sixty (60) days' prior written notice. Landlord may terminate this Lease for cause if Tenant materially breaches any provision and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days of written notice. Tenant may terminate this Lease early if the premises become uninhabitable due to conditions not caused by Tenant, after providing reasonable written notice and an opportunity for Landlord to remedy.
sourceAttribution: Based on HUD model lease and tenant rights organizations' recommendations

clauseText: Indemnification. Tenant shall indemnify and hold Landlord harmless from and against claims arising from Tenant's negligence or willful misconduct in the use of the premises. Landlord shall indemnify and hold Tenant harmless from claims arising from Landlord's failure to maintain the premises in a habitable condition or from hazardous conditions in common areas under Landlord's control. Neither party shall be required to indemnify the other for claims arising from the other party's own negligence.
sourceAttribution: Based on balanced residential lease templates from tenant advocacy groups

clauseText: Privacy. Landlord shall respect Tenant's right to quiet enjoyment of the premises. Landlord or Landlord's agents shall provide at least twenty-four (24) hours' advance written notice before entering the premises, except in cases of emergency. Landlord shall not disclose Tenant's personal or financial information to third parties except as required by law or as necessary for property management purposes.
sourceAttribution: Based on HUD model lease and state tenant privacy protections

clauseText: Governing Law. This Lease shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the premises are located, including all applicable landlord-tenant statutes and local housing ordinances. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this Lease and applicable law, the provisions of applicable law shall prevail. Both parties acknowledge that Tenant may have rights under local and state law that cannot be waived by agreement.
sourceAttribution: Based on HUD model lease provisions

clauseText: Dispute Resolution. In the event of any dispute arising under this Lease, the parties shall first attempt to resolve the matter through good-faith negotiation. If negotiation fails, either party may seek mediation through a local community mediation center. Nothing in this section shall prevent either party from seeking emergency relief or pursuing claims in small claims court. The prevailing party in any legal action shall be entitled to recover reasonable attorneys' fees.
sourceAttribution: Based on balanced residential lease dispute resolution

clauseText: Condition of Premises. Landlord represents and warrants that the premises are in a habitable condition and comply with all applicable building codes, health regulations, and safety standards at the time of lease commencement. Landlord shall maintain the structural components, plumbing, electrical systems, heating, and common areas in good repair throughout the lease term. Tenant shall maintain the premises in a clean and sanitary condition and promptly report any maintenance issues to Landlord.
sourceAttribution: Based on HUD model lease and implied warranty of habitability

clauseText: Force Majeure. Neither party shall be liable for failure to perform obligations under this Lease (other than the payment of rent) due to causes beyond reasonable control, including natural disasters, government orders, or utility failures. If force majeure conditions render the premises uninhabitable for more than thirty (30) days, Tenant may terminate this Lease without penalty and shall receive a pro-rated refund of any prepaid rent.
sourceAttribution: Based on balanced residential lease force majeure provisions

clauseText: Assignment and Subletting. Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet the premises without Landlord's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. If Landlord consents to a sublease, Tenant shall remain liable under this Lease unless expressly released in writing. Landlord may not unreasonably refuse a proposed subtenant who meets the same qualification criteria applied to Tenant.
sourceAttribution: Based on balanced residential subletting provisions

clauseText: Notices. All notices required under this Lease shall be in writing and shall be deemed delivered when personally delivered, sent by certified mail (return receipt requested), or sent by email with read receipt to the addresses provided in this Lease. Landlord shall also post any legally required notices at the premises. Either party may change its notice address upon thirty (30) days' written notice to the other party.
sourceAttribution: Based on standard residential lease notice provisions

clauseText: Amendments. This Lease may not be modified except by a written amendment signed by both Landlord and Tenant. No oral agreements or representations shall be binding upon either party. Any changes to the rent amount, lease term, or material terms shall require a written amendment executed by both parties at least thirty (30) days before the change takes effect.
sourceAttribution: Based on standard residential lease amendment provisions

clauseText: Limitation of Liability. Landlord's liability for damages arising from breach of this Lease or negligence shall be limited to direct damages actually incurred by Tenant. Landlord shall not be liable for consequential, incidental, or punitive damages except in cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct. Nothing in this section shall limit Landlord's obligations under applicable habitability laws or Tenant's right to seek statutory remedies.
sourceAttribution: Based on balanced residential lease liability provisions

clauseText: Insurance. Landlord shall maintain property insurance covering the structure and common areas of the premises. Tenant is encouraged, but not required, to obtain renter's insurance covering personal property and personal liability. If Tenant obtains renter's insurance, Tenant may be asked to add Landlord as an interested party. Neither party shall be liable for losses covered by the other party's insurance policy to the extent of such coverage.
sourceAttribution: Based on balanced residential lease insurance provisions

clauseText: Use of Premises. The premises shall be used exclusively for residential purposes. Tenant shall not use the premises for any unlawful purpose or in any manner that creates a nuisance or disturbs other residents. Tenant may make minor decorative changes (painting, hanging pictures) without Landlord's consent but shall restore the premises to their original condition upon move-out, normal wear and tear excepted. Any structural modifications require Landlord's prior written consent.
sourceAttribution: Based on HUD model lease permitted use provisions

clauseText: Security Deposit. Landlord shall hold the security deposit in a separate interest-bearing account as required by applicable law. The security deposit shall be returned to Tenant within thirty (30) days of lease termination, less any amounts lawfully deducted for unpaid rent, damages beyond normal wear and tear, or other charges permitted by this Lease. Landlord shall provide an itemized statement of any deductions. The security deposit shall not exceed the amount permitted by applicable law.
sourceAttribution: Based on HUD model lease and state security deposit statutes

clauseText: Renewal Terms. At the end of the initial lease term, this Lease shall automatically renew on a month-to-month basis under the same terms and conditions, unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. Landlord may propose adjusted rent for any renewal period by providing at least sixty (60) days' written notice before the renewal date. Tenant may decline the adjustment and terminate upon thirty (30) days' notice.
sourceAttribution: Based on balanced residential lease renewal provisions
